messages:
ops-incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER — Elevated 5xx and degraded outputs for EU inference traffic. Symptoms: requests intended for model variant 'gpt-medium-avx' are being served the smaller 'gpt-small-quant' variant due to cache/routing mismatch. Affected: routing-service, kv-cache. Start time ~2024-11-04T09:35Z. Runbook: https://wiki.redwood/incident/runbooks/kv-routing

priya: I'm on call and taking ownership. tagging @alex for on-shift handoff. Any immediate customer-facing mitigation?

alex: I noticed a spike at ~09:30UTC, thought it was a transient deploy. Seeing mismatched cache entries in logs:
```
time=2024-11-04T09:31:02Z level=info svc=routing service_request_id=xyz cache_key="eu|model=gpt-medium-avx|prefix=v2" cache_value="gpt-small-quant|node:eu-3"
```
That cache_value shouldn't be for that cache_key. Suspect prefix normalization change in last routing release.

tim: Pinged. I pulled the routing-config diff from the release this morning: https://git.redwood/repo/commit/7a9f2d -> changed model alias normalization. Code snippet:
```go
// old
routeKey := fmt.Sprintf("%s:%s", region, model.ID)
// new
routeKey := fmt.Sprintf("%s:%s", region, normalizeAlias(model.Alias))
```
normalizeAlias strips suffixes like "-avx" in some cases, so model IDs and aliases no longer align with kv prefixing.

priya: Ok. Immediate plan: disable cross-region prefix cache writes for eu namespace and fall back to direct routing (no cached variant). Executing admin toggle now.
`curl -s -X POST "https://admin.redwood/api/cache/namespace/eu/ttl?write_enabled=false" -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED"`

deploy-bot: admin action accepted, namespace=eu, write_enabled=false, timestamp=2024-11-04T09:38:10Z

priya: After disabling writes, I'm purging existing eu prefix namespace (soft purge).
`curl -s -X POST "https://admin.redwood/api/cache/namespace/eu/purge?mode=soft"`

ops-incident-bot: Auto-scaling fallback observed for routing-service in eu: instances scaled +3 to handle fallback load. No CPU OOMs reported.

lina: Product note: Support has 6 incoming tickets from EU customers complaining about inconsistent outputs. Which customers saw degraded output vs outright errors? Can we surface list?

alex: Querying request logs for error signature and model mismatch tag. Sample:
```
2024-11-04T09:33:05Z request_id=abc user=customer-42 model_requested=gpt-medium-avx model_served=gpt-small-quant status=200 confidence=low
```
Most are silent degradations (returned 200 but wrong size/quality). Couple of real 5xxs where downstream expected larger payload.

tim: Suggest a targeted rollback of the alias-normalization change in routing-config for eu region only (canary). I have a rollback patch ready: https://git.redwood/repo/pr/432/rollback-normalize. Command to apply canary:
```
kubectl apply -f routing-config-eu-canary.yaml --context=cluster-eu
```
Will reduce cache-key mismatch risk while we fix normalization logic and update kv-prefixing.

priya: Applying canary rollback now to 2/6 routers in eu.
`kubectl apply -f routing-config-eu-canary.yaml --context=cluster-eu -n routing --record`

priya: Canary rolled out to 2 routers at 09:47UTC. Monitoring metrics.

alex: Quick redis inspection shows mixed key formats:
```
redis> SCAN 0 MATCH "eu:*" COUNT 1000
1) "0"
2) 1) "eu:gpt-medium-avx:v2"
   2) "eu:gpt-medium:v2"
   3) "eu:gpt_small-quant:v2"
```
Looks like both 'gpt-medium-avx' and 'gpt-medium' keys existed and some write paths wrote the wrong value into the common namespace.

tim: Canary rollback in canary routers applied. I'm rolling back the normalization change from the routing code in the EU cluster now. Will also coordinate a short config migration to make the key format explicit: add model_id + explicit variant tag.

priya: Metrics update 09:52UTC: 5xx rate in eu down from 12.3% -> 1.1% after disabling writes and canary rollback. Latency stable. Post-rollback we see correct variant served on canary routers.

ops-incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Pager auto-clear check pending. If no regression in next 15m, consider incident mitigated.

lina: Customer comms: I'll draft a note for impacted customers summarizing issue and mitigations. Priya, can you confirm list of affected customer ids and time windows?

priya: Will compile list and push to #customer-notifications in 20m. Taking incident lead for postmortem.

alex: Root cause hypothesis: routing alias normalization introduced inconsistency between the routing key used to select a model variant and the kv-cache key generation. This allowed stale/incorrect entries to be reused, occasionally pointing to a smaller variant. Remediation: revert normalization change + make kv-prefix explicit (region:model_id:variant) and add validation in write path.

tim: Agreed. I'll open an immediate PR with conservative key format migration + tests to prevent alias/ID divergence. Also adding a health-check that asserts cache_value.model == model_selected at write time for 10% of writes.

priya: Incident update: declaring mitigated at 10:10UTC after 18 minutes of stable metrics post-rollback. Creating incident ticket and scheduling postmortem for tomorrow 14:00UTC. CC: routing, kv-cache, runtime, support.

ops-incident-bot: Incident state: mitigated -> postmortem_required. Runbook link: https://wiki.redwood/incident/1865432100-kv-prefix-misdirect

priya: Assigning postmortem owners: tim (runtime), alex (sre/routing), lina (customer impact). I'll collect timeline and logs, and include suggested action items: revert live, explicit key format, migration plan, add canary guardrails.

deploy-bot: action=rollback commit=7a9f2d -> rollback applied to cluster-eu canary at 2024-11-04T09:48:12Z

priya: Thanks everyone. I'll keep thread updated with postmortem doc once created. :thumbsup:
